title: Dishonour of cheque (s.138 NI Act)
text: Cheque returned unpaid for insufficient funds is an offence punishable with up to 2 years prison or fine up to twice the cheque amount. Send a demand notice within 30 days of the return memo; the drawer has 15 days to pay; file the complaint within one month after that period.

title: Consumer complaint to District Commission
citation: Consumer Protection Act 2019, s.35 and s.69
text: A consumer can file a complaint about defective goods or deficient services with the District Consumer Commission, online through e-Daakhil. The complaint must be filed within two years from the cause of action.

title: Information in cognisable cases (FIR)
text: Information about a cognisable offence can be given orally, in writing or electronically to the police, who must register it and give the informant a free copy. Zero FIR can be registered at any station regardless of jurisdiction.

title: Anticipatory bail
text: A person who fears arrest for a non-bailable offence may apply to the High Court or Court of Session for a direction to be released on bail if arrested.

title: Cheating
text: Dishonestly deceiving a person to deliver property or to act to their loss is cheating, punishable with imprisonment and fine; cheating that induces delivery of property carries up to 7 years. Replaces IPC s.415 and s.420.

title: Murder
text: Murder is punishable with death or imprisonment for life, and fine. Replaces IPC s.302.

title: Compensation for breach of contract
text: The party who suffers from a breach is entitled to compensation for loss that naturally arose from the breach or that both parties knew was likely. Remote or indirect loss is not compensated.

title: Valid contract
text: Agreements are contracts if made with free consent of competent parties, for a lawful consideration and a lawful object, and not expressly declared void.

title: Termination of tenancy notice
text: A month-to-month tenancy can be ended by 15 days written notice and a year-to-year tenancy by 6 months notice, unless the contract or local rent law says otherwise. A landlord cannot evict without following due process.

title: Divorce by mutual consent
text: Spouses living separately for one year or more who cannot live together can jointly petition for divorce. A second motion is made after a cooling period of 6 to 18 months.

title: Limitation period for suits
text: A suit filed after the prescribed period is dismissed even if the claim is valid. Most money recovery and breach of contract suits must be filed within 3 years.

title: Electronic evidence
text: Electronic records such as emails, chats and call logs are admissible if accompanied by the required certificate. Replaces s.65B of the Indian Evidence Act.

title: Domestic violence relief
citation: Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act 2005, s.12
text: An aggrieved woman can apply to a Magistrate for protection orders, residence orders, monetary relief and custody orders.

title: Protection of life and personal liberty
text: No person can be deprived of life or personal liberty except by a procedure established by law, and that procedure must be fair, just and reasonable. Includes the right to speedy trial and legal aid.

title: Arnesh Kumar v. State of Bihar
text: Arrest is not automatic for offences punishable up to 7 years. Police must record reasons for arrest and Magistrates must check them before authorising detention. Relevant to bail and wrongful arrest.

title: Lalita Kumari v. Govt. of U.P.
text: Police must register an FIR when information discloses a cognisable offence. A preliminary inquiry is allowed only in limited categories such as matrimonial, commercial and medical negligence cases.

title: Maneka Gandhi v. Union of India
text: The procedure that restricts personal liberty under Article 21 must be fair, just and reasonable, not arbitrary. Articles 14, 19 and 21 are read together.

title: Amardeep Singh v. Harveen Kaur
text: The 6 month cooling period in mutual consent divorce under s.13B(2) is directory and courts may waive it where reconciliation is impossible and the parties have settled all issues.

title: Indian Medical Association v. V.P. Shantha
text: Medical services paid for are services under consumer law, so patients can claim compensation for deficiency in service or negligence before consumer forums.

title: Vishaka v. State of Rajasthan
text: The Supreme Court laid down binding guidelines to prevent sexual harassment of women at the workplace, later codified in the POSH Act 2013.

title: Gurbaksh Singh Sibbia v. State of Punjab
text: Anticipatory bail should not be hedged by rigid conditions. Courts decide on the facts of each case, considering the nature of the accusation and likelihood of absconding.

title: Rangappa v. Sri Mohan
text: Under s.139 NI Act the court presumes a cheque was issued for a legally enforceable debt. The accused can rebut it by showing the debt probably did not exist.

title: Arjun Panditrao Khotkar v. Kailash Kushanrao Gorantyal
text: A certificate under s.65B(4) of the Evidence Act is mandatory to admit electronic evidence given as a copy. Same principle now sits in s.63 BSA.
